exposure: first and second stages of labor
outcome: probability of OPP detection at birth
cohort: uncomplicated cephalic single foetus pregnant women at term
finding: Assessing fetal spinal position during labor, particularly concordant posterior positions, can predict delivery outcomes, with longer labor, increased analgesia requests, and higher rates of operative delivery and cesarean sections.
mod_finding: This study found that fetal occiput posterior position during labor was associated with a higher likelihood of cesarean section and operative vaginal deliveries.
